creature_families: Monster rows by race trait: humanoid 904, undead 576, beast 256, construct 247, demonic 222, insect 205, animal 202, divine 92, spirit 87, plant 53, fairy 51, dragon 37, giant 14; 1400 rows carry no race trait. (data/Npcs/*.json, traits.race)

Escalation by 10-level band, median max HP of Monster rows: band 0-9 about 90, 10-19 about 302, 20-29 about 592, 30-39 about 1109, 40-49 about 1660, 50-59 about 1829, 60-69 about 3626, 70-79 about 4229, 80-89 about 4663. Median physical attack rises about 180x from the first band (12) to the last (2148). Shape only, no stat blocks copied.

Raid bosses: 179 raid-flagged rows, levels 20 to 67, in data/Npcs/c4_raid_bosses.json and data/Npcs/c4_low_level_raid_bosses.json. Each boss has a linked minion list (284 rows, bossId field) in data/Npcs/Minions/c4_raid_bosses.json.
Summoned servants: 194 Summon rows. data/Npcs/PHANTOM_SUMMONS.md describes three summoner families across 50 skill levels, with their own behaviours (absorb, corpse burst, poison ticks).
Role tags as data: data/Npcs/ai.json maps every NPC id to FIGHTER, ARCHER or BALANCED (one line, read).

top_creatures.label: Corpse-burst husk
top_creatures.why: A summoned servant (the Soulless family in the doc) whose signature is a burst centred on a corpse it consumes, plus a toxic smoke cloud. One clear behaviour; the burst ring is the cue that would read at 375 wide. Sound and art not read (no audio or art in the donor).
top_creatures.keep: Corpse as a combat object; area burst from the body; one gimmick per summon family.
top_creatures.change: Our own burst ring, art, name and sound; the smoke becomes our own status field.
top_creatures.ref: data/Npcs/PHANTOM_SUMMONS.md line 27 (Soulless: corpse burst, toxic smoke) and line 33 (corpse-centred area damage with corpse consumption)

top_creatures.label: Blood-drinking shade
top_creatures.why: A summoner servant family (Silhouette in the doc) whose Steal Blood heals it on hit; the doc's runtime checks list 20% steal-blood absorption and 15% melee absorption. Heal-on-hit gives a readable tell (a drain tendril) without a new brain.
top_creatures.keep: Heal-on-hit as the signature; absorb numbers as data, not code.
top_creatures.change: Our shade silhouette and the drain visual; absorb values set per zone.
top_creatures.ref: data/Npcs/PHANTOM_SUMMONS.md line 27 (Silhouette: Steal Blood) and line 32 (absorb checks)

top_creatures.label: Warband warden
top_creatures.why: A raid boss that brings its own linked minion list. A boss plus a wave of minions gives a readable phase at a glance (boss height plus a ring of smaller figures). Raid bosses number 179 across levels 20-67.
top_creatures.keep: Boss plus a separate minion list keyed by boss id; minions load as data; the cold-fight code reads the same list.
top_creatures.change: Our boss silhouette and palette; our minion roster; our wave timing.

top_creatures.label: Great wyrm tier
top_creatures.why: Dragon-race rows sit at the top of the level range (dragon rows run levels 34 to 85). Scarce, late and large: a readable boss-tier silhouette if the wing span is the cue.
top_creatures.keep: Dragons only in the top bands; a few per zone; one large-collision body.
top_creatures.change: Our own wyrm silhouette, element and sound; no shared name or shape.
top_creatures.ref: data/Npcs/c4_forge_of_the_gods.json line 1096 (dragon race trait, level 85 rows); data/Npcs/c4_legacy_monsters.json (10 dragon rows)

top_creatures.label: Colossus band
top_creatures.why: Giant-race rows (14) sit alone in levels 61-65, a small late set. Scale alone reads at 375 wide, which suits a big-body beast in our roster.
top_creatures.keep: Few giants, one band, large collision radius.
top_creatures.change: Our own giant body, pose and attack; no copied silhouette.
top_creatures.ref: data/Npcs/npcs.json line 7822 (giant race trait row); data/Npcs/c4_legacy_monsters.json (giant rows also present)

top_creatures.label: Hive swarm
top_creatures.why: Insect-race rows (205) spread across levels 15-81 and sit in dungeon-type files. A large insect family gives a swarm shape that reads as a crowd, not a single boss.
top_creatures.keep: Insect family across many bands; many small bodies per encounter.
top_creatures.change: Our own insect shapes, sounds and a swarm cap set per zone.

top_creatures.label: Restless dead
top_creatures.why: Undead-race rows (576) are the largest family and cover levels 1-82. A large family across the whole curve gives a clear first-to-last progression for a single creature theme.
top_creatures.keep: One theme across all bands, with a tier per band.
top_creatures.change: Our own dead silhouettes and tier cues; no shared name.
top_creatures.ref: undead race trait rows in data/Npcs/c4_catacomb_of_*.json, data/Npcs/c4_devastated_castle.json, data/Npcs/c4_devils_isle.json, data/Npcs/c4_fields_of_silence_and_whispers.json (and others)

top_creatures.label: Sprite trickster
top_creatures.why: Fairy-race rows (51) sit across levels 1-78 and include the lowest-level monsters. A light, fast family reads well as a contrast to heavy bosses.
top_creatures.keep: Fast small body; trickster movement; many at the low bands.
top_creatures.change: Our own sprite silhouette, colour and sound.
top_creatures.ref: data/Npcs/npcs.json line 4 (fairy race trait, first template in the file)

classes: Root tier (9 root class ids, no parent): each carries a skill tree of 9-37 skills in data/Skills/Tree/tree.json. Role: not stated in the data. Progression: first promotion.
First-profession tier (18 ids): children of the roots, 1-3 per root (firstProfMap, src/GameServer/ClassProgression.js line 35). Mechanic: a new skill set on promotion.
Second-profession tier (31 ids): children of the first tier (secondProfMap, line 47). Mechanic: a second promotion with its own skills.

Third-class tier (31 ids, ids 88-118): each has a base combat-point cap and a per-level add (base about 1049 to 2756; per-level add about 21 to 57, one shared modifier of 0.22). Progression: combat points grow per level; the lineage walk (line 94) finds the parent chain.

NPC roles (not classes): FIGHTER, ARCHER or BALANCED per NPC id in data/Npcs/ai.json. The cold-combat class policy requires a BotRoles module (src/GameServer/Bot/Population/ColdClassPolicy.js line 3); that module was not read, so whether it reads ai.json is not checked.
weapon_families: Weapon kinds (861 rows in data/Items/Weapons): blunt 210, sword 136, dual 117, knife 95, pole 76, bow 64, dual-fist 52, misc 42, great sword 30, pet 30, fist 9.
Rank tiers on weapons: none 136, d 122, c 304, b 146, a 100, s 53 (data/Items/Weapons/weapons.json etc., field etc.rank).

Special abilities: data/Items/weapon_sa.json lists 443 weapons with conditional stat blocks and 36 proc definitions. Proc families: drain 7, poison 3, bleed 3, stun 2, silence 2, root 1, slow 1, others 17 (buffs, curses, magic holds).

Conditional bonuses: 79 conditional stat entries in weapon_sa.json; the one read example is gated by minEnchantLevel 4. The test notes cover a +4 dual case (WEAPON_SA.md line 124). Gate types other than enchant were not counted.
Pole and bow ranges: explicit pole range and angle preserved in the SA generator (WEAPON_SA.md line 13).
gear_tiers: Armour kinds (809 rows in data/Items/Armors): wear 366, jewel 113, fabric 87, shield 76, chain 71, leather 66, pet 30.
Rank tiers: none 142, d 103, c 103, b 279, a 134, s 48.

Sealed and unsealed grades: c4_sealed_a_grade 23 rows, c4_unsealed 38 rows, c4_a_grade 9, c4_b_grade 24, c4_s_grade 20. An exchange recipe list (data/Items/c4_unseal.json) turns sealed pieces into unsealed ones, a state reveal rather than a visual swap.

Soul-crystal ladder for weapons: 3 colours, stages 0-13, 42 intact crystals plus broken remains (data/Items/SOUL_CRYSTALS.md line 3). Stage 13 is terminal (SOUL_CRYSTALS.md line 26). Install needs the weapon and the exact colour and stage of crystal (WEAPON_SA.md lines 63-68).
How tiers show: rank letters in data, sealed or unsealed state, and the crystal stage. Client rendering not read (no client in donor).
zones: Catacomb-type dungeons: 6 files (data/Npcs/c4_catacomb_of_*.json), each with its own spawn set and reward table in data/Npcs/Rewards/.
Necropolis chain: 8 files (data/Npcs/c4_necropolis_of_*.json), a themed graveyard series.

Field and island zones: alligator island, swamp of screams, fields of silence, garden of beasts, hot springs, valley of saints, wall of argos, maille lizardmen, and others (about 25 files in data/Npcs/c4_*.json).
Raid lairs: c4_raid_bosses.json (174 rows) and c4_low_level_raid_bosses.json (5 rows) with minion lists.
Town and service zones: town NPC files, guild and clan-hall files (ClanHallManager rows 50 across the Npcs files), teleport table of 34 entries (data/Teleports/teleports.json).

World spawn file: data/Npcs/Spawns/spawns.json holds 13,465 spawn groups covering 26,945 mobs; respawn median 95 s, with common values 15, 60, 240 and 10800 s. The bias field takes 0, 15, 50, 120 and 180 (meaning not read). Some respawn values are -1 or 950400 (sentinels, not explained in the read files).
Hazards: not read as a table (no trap table in the donor; the donor's own README was read for tiers only).

looks.label: Pixel crest badges
looks.technique: Indexed-colour bitmap badges at fixed small sizes (8 x 12 for ally crests, 16 x 12 for clan crests), 485 files in total. Pixel art reads well at small size on a phone.
looks.ref: data/crests/ally and data/crests/clan; data/crests/README.md line 6 (16 x 12 size)

looks.label: Sealed-to-open reveal
looks.technique: A state change on an item (sealed to unsealed by recipe) rather than a shader. Reveal moment as a gameplay step.
looks.ref: data/Items/c4_unseal.json (exchange recipe list, 38 armour rows in data/Items/Armors/c4_unsealed.json)

looks.label: Summon corpse ring
looks.technique: Area burst centred on a corpse, with a smoke effect. Effect art not read (no client); described from the server doc only.

looks.label: Proc name effects
looks.technique: Critical procs show as named special abilities (poison, bleed, drain, stun). The visual per proc is not in the server half.

originals.name: Corpse Reliquary
originals.idea: A summoner's servant that drains the fallen: it spends a corpse to burst outward in a ring, then leaves a short smoke field.
originals.keep: Corpse as a combat resource; a single burst ring as the signature; a smoke field as the after-effect.
originals.change: Our own silhouette, element, ring art and sound; poison becomes our own status with its own duration.

originals.name: Warband Standard
originals.idea: A boss that plants its standard and calls a linked wave of smaller fighters, keyed by the boss id.
originals.keep: Boss plus a separate minion list keyed by boss id; a timed wave.
originals.change: Our boss body and palette; our minion roster; wave timing and a visible standard on the boss.

originals.name: Tidewake Shade
originals.idea: A drain-type servant: each landed hit returns a share of damage as healing to its summoner.
originals.keep: Heal-on-hit as the signature; absorb numbers live in data.
originals.change: Our own shade silhouette, drain tendril visual, and absorb caps per zone.

originals.name: Ember Proc Blade
originals.idea: A weapon whose critical hits roll a damage-over-time proc (poison or bleed), separate from the target's resist roll.
originals.keep: Procs on critical only; proc chance separate from resist; no proc on skills or misses.
originals.change: Our own proc names and effects; a distinct glow per proc family.

originals.name: Stage Ladder Relic
originals.idea: A gear item that grows one stage at a time when fed a matching crystal, with a small chance to break and a terminal top stage.
originals.keep: Exact colour and stage match; growth and break odds; a terminal stage that cannot grow.
originals.change: Our own odds (the donor's numbers are a compatibility baseline, not verified); our own stage names and colours.

originals.name: Band Warden Pack
originals.idea: A zone population where a few top-band bosses hold the far zone and cheap background actors fill the rest, promoted to full detail on approach.
originals.keep: Three tiers by distance; promotion on approach; a background loop that keeps goals; budgets that tighten when a player is near.
originals.change: Our tier names and distances; a fight-only tier that is always full. Maps to parity row 23 (zone population) and row 18 (per-tick NPC budget).
